title: Partition Results
prompt: A TypeScript batch job returns success and error results together. Write a function that separates them into { success, error } arrays while preserving the original order within each group.

explanation.beginner:
Example: partitionResults([{"status":"success","id":"1"},{"status":"error","id":"2","message":"Nope"}]) produces {"success":[{"status":"success","id":"1"}],"error":[{"status":"error","id":"2","message":"Nope"}]}. Create separate result buckets and route each input to exactly one according to its predicate.

Compare “handles no results”: input [[]] produces {"success":[],"error":[]}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Create separate result buckets and route each input to exactly one according to its predicate.

Tempting mistake: Two unrelated filters can drift apart and accidentally drop or duplicate records. Check that the partition preserves the input count.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles no results”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
